Diabetes Mental Health Support

Psychological Support for Living with Diabetes

Diabetes mental health support focuses on practical strategies to reduce emotional burden and improve daily coping. Sessions address stress management, mood regulation, problem-solving, diabetes-related anxiety, and adherence challenges . The aim is to strengthen resilience, restore energy for self-care, and improve quality of life alongside medical treatment. Michelle Barratt Psychology (MBP) provides in-person therapy across Brisbane, and flexible online therapy options Australia-wide, ensuring your healing journey remains consistent and accessible.

How does MBP support Diabetes Mental Health?

Michelle Barratt Psychology and Administrative Services provides a clinically informed administrative hub for clients, independent psychologists, and the wider medical team in Brisbane and across Australia . Our administration ensures seamless coordination between you, your psychologist, and your diabetes care providers so clinical communication is clear, timely, and respectful. This coordination preserves clinician objectivity while helping medical and mental health professionals work together effectively.

If you are dealing with the emotional burden of diabetes, please don't hesitate to email us or contact us to find out how we can assist you.

How do I get started?

We can connect you with experienced Brisbane psychologists who specialise in chronic illness, health psychology, and diabetes distress. If you would like help finding a practitioner or arranging coordinated care, please email us to discuss options and referrals. You may also view our Practitioner Page to choose a clinician directly.

Important safety note

If you are in immediate danger, experiencing severe distress, or having thoughts of harming yourself, contact emergency services or a crisis service right away. If you are concerned but not in immediate danger, please mention this when you contact us so we can prioritise an appropriate, timely response.

The Emotional Impact of Living with Diabetes

Managing diabetes requires ongoing attention, planning, and decision-making. Over time, the responsibility of monitoring blood sugar levels, attending medical appointments, managing medication, and maintaining lifestyle changes can become emotionally exhausting.

Many people living with diabetes experience periods of frustration, stress, anxiety, or low mood. It is common to feel overwhelmed at times, particularly following diagnosis, during life transitions, or when facing complications and health concerns. Psychological support can help individuals develop coping strategies and maintain emotional wellbeing alongside their physical health care.

Diabetes and Mental Health

Living with diabetes may contribute to a range of emotional and psychological challenges, including:

  • Anxiety about health and future complications
  • Feelings of stress or overwhelm
  • Diabetes-related burnout
  • Low mood or depression
  • Difficulty maintaining motivation
  • Fear of blood sugar fluctuations
  • Emotional exhaustion from ongoing self-management
  • Reduced confidence in managing health needs

Support from a psychologist can help individuals navigate these challenges and build practical coping strategies.

What is Diabetes Burnout?

Diabetes burnout refers to the emotional exhaustion that can develop when the demands of managing diabetes become overwhelming. Individuals may feel frustrated, discouraged, exhausted, or disconnected from their treatment routines.

Burnout can make it more difficult to maintain healthy habits, attend appointments, or engage in ongoing diabetes management. Therapy can help individuals address these feelings, regain motivation, and develop sustainable approaches to managing both their physical and emotional well-being.

How Therapy Can Help

Psychological support can play an important role in helping individuals adapt to life with diabetes. Therapy may focus on:

  • Managing anxiety and stress
  • Developing healthy coping strategies
  • Improving emotional resilience
  • Supporting behaviour change and motivation
  • Addressing low mood and depression
  • Managing health-related worries
  • Strengthening self-care routines
  • Improving overall quality of life

Therapy complements medical care by supporting the emotional and psychological aspects of living with a chronic health condition.

Living with diabetes is often easier when individuals feel supported by those around them. With the right guidance, families and carers can develop practical strategies that support both their loved one's wellbeing and their own.

Supporting a Loved One Living with Diabetes

A diabetes diagnosis can affect the whole family. Parents, partners, spouses, and carers often play an important role in supporting treatment routines, managing appointments, and helping loved ones navigate the emotional challenges associated with diabetes.

Providing support can sometimes be stressful, particularly when family members worry about health outcomes, treatment adherence, or the long-term impact of the condition. Family members may also experience their own feelings of anxiety, frustration, or emotional fatigue.

Accessing appropriate support can help families better understand diabetes, improve communication, and create a more supportive environment for everyone involved.

1 Diabetes Education

2 Communication Skills

Develop supportive and constructive ways to discuss health concerns.

3 Emotional Support

4 Healthy Boundaries

5 Stress Management
